name: Donald Trump
quote: NATO is absolutely useless. I would have liked your help two months ago, but now I really don't want your help anymore — they were absolutely useless when we needed them. STAY AWAY. [May 7: White House CT strategy labels Europe a 'terror incubator.' May 26 (Der Spiegel exclusive): Pentagon adviser Velez-Green secretly notified European NATO allies at a confidential Brussels meeting of sweeping military contribution reductions — fighter jets minus one-third, bombers halved, zero submarines, zero drones, warships reduced — on top of 10,200+ confirmed troop cuts. European attendees reportedly 'shocked' at the scope. Gap-filling plan demanded by Ankara (July 7–8).]

name: Joe Biden
quote: America is back. The transatlantic alliance is back. And we are not looking backward; we are looking forward, together.

name: Emmanuel Macron
quote: EU Article 42.7 is, in substance, stronger than Article 5 — it leaves no option. The lesson we must draw is: let us no longer be dependent. We Europeans must strengthen this European pillar of NATO — not against anyone, not as an alternative to anything. [May 28: Macron and Norwegian PM Støre signed the Narvik Agreement in Paris — extending France's nuclear deterrence guarantee to Norway, making it the 9th European country under French extended deterrence. Named for the 1940 Battle of Narvik, the pact covers mutual military assistance, nuclear umbrella extension, defense industrial integration, and High North/Arctic intelligence sharing.]

name: Jens Stoltenberg
quote: It's not a natural law that we will have NATO forever. It's not written in stone that NATO will exist for the next ten years. I urge allies and the US Senate to take these threats seriously.

name: Mark Rutte
quote: NATO is ready to defend every inch of allied territory. Russia's reckless behavior poses a danger to us all — last night once again showed that the consequences of their illegal war of aggression do not end at the border. [June 1: Romania's official investigation confirmed the Galati drone = Russian Geran-2, eliminating Russia's 'blame Ukraine' deflection. NATO and Romania discussing Article 4 consultation — a formal NAC meeting on threats to alliance territorial integrity. Rutte: 'We will defend every inch, and we continue to review all options in coordination with Romania.' May 31: US expected to submit formal NATO European force-level withdrawal plan in June. NATO MEROPS counter-drone integration for Romania proceeding. May 29: Rutte called Romanian President Dan after the Galati drone strike — first civilian casualties from a Russian drone strike on NATO territory. No Article 5 invocation. May 22 Helsingborg: 'The question is not whether we need to do more, but how quickly we turn commitments into capabilities.' Next: Ankara Leaders' Summit July 7–8, 2026.]

name: Ursula von der Leyen
quote: Let's develop our strength without constantly leaning on someone else. Europe is in a fight — a fight for a continent that is whole and at peace.

name: Olaf Scholz
quote: We need a powerful, cutting-edge, progressive Bundeswehr. This Zeitenwende — this turning point — demands our joint effort. There will be a special fund of €100 billion for the Bundeswehr.

name: Friedrich Merz
quote: Tehran is humiliating the Trump administration. The blockade may be forcing negotiations, but Washington has alienated every ally it needed — that is a strategic failure, not a success. Europe must now build its own strength without waiting to be invited.

name: Mette Frederiksen
quote: If the United States chooses to attack another NATO country militarily, then everything stops — that is, including our NATO, and thus the security that has been provided since the end of the Second World War.

name: JD Vance
quote: I genuinely believe that the greatest threat to the security of Europe is not Russia. The greatest threat to the security of Europe is from within — it is the retreat from the values that make Western civilisation worth defending.

name: Volodymyr Zelensky
quote: It's unprecedented and absurd when a timeframe is not set, neither for the invitation nor for Ukraine's membership, while at the same time allies are represented as open to inviting Ukraine.

name: Recep Tayyip Erdoğan
quote: Turkey is working to revive Russia-Ukraine peace negotiations. We are ready to play our role as a facilitating party ahead of the Ankara Summit. Turkey is a committed NATO ally and will contribute to the alliance's defense production agenda.

name: James Mattis
quote: America will meet its Article 5 commitments. But if your nation does not want to see America moderate its commitment to this alliance, each of your capitals needs to show support for our common defense.

name: Andrzej Duda
quote: Poland is the most credible NATO ally — we spend over 4% of GDP on defense and we want a permanent, full American military base on Polish soil. We are ready to pay for it. We call it Fort Trump.

name: Kaja Kallas
role: EU Foreign Policy Chief / former Estonian PM (2024–present)
quote: The EU has always supported attempts to achieve a just and lasting peace. For Europe to take a more active role, we must agree amongst ourselves what we want to talk to Russia about and what our red lines are. [May 12, 2026: EU FAC Defence, Brussels — chairing the emergency defence ministerial as NATO and EU run dual emergency tracks toward Helsingborg and Ankara.]

name: Boris Johnson
quote: The UK stands four-square behind Article 5 and NATO's collective defense obligation. Brexit has not changed our commitment to European security — if anything it makes our NATO engagement more important, not less.

name: Rishi Sunak
quote: The United Kingdom is committed to spending 2.5% of GDP on defense. We must ensure NATO remains the cornerstone of our collective defense while European nations do more to carry their share of the burden.

name: Keir Starmer
quote: The UK has a proud history of leadership in NATO and we will continue to invest in our security. We are committed to reaching 2.5% of GDP on defense and will work with our European partners to strengthen the alliance. [May 27: Starmer and Polish PM Tusk signed the Northolt Treaty at RAF Northolt — the bilateral defense pact covering missile systems, drone technologies, defense industrial collaboration, and cybersecurity. Starmer called it 'the most fitting place we could have chosen — where Polish and British service members fought side by side and changed the course of history.']

name: Angela Merkel
quote: The times in which we could rely fully on others are somewhat over, as I experienced in the last few days. We Europeans must really take our destiny into our own hands. We must fight for our own future as Europeans.

name: Donald Tusk
role: Polish Prime Minister (2023–present) / former European Council President
quote: I know from Polish experience what Russia truly is. That's why Poland invests more than 4% of GDP in defense. We don't need lectures about burden-sharing — we are the most credible NATO ally on the eastern flank. [May 27: Tusk and UK PM Starmer signed the Northolt Treaty at RAF Northolt — where Polish pilots of the 303 Squadron flew in the Battle of Britain. Warsaw has now signed bilateral defense compacts with London, Paris, and Kyiv, completing a trilateral network covering three of Europe's largest defense budgets.]

name: Marco Rubio
quote: Like any alliance, it has to be good for everyone who's involved. There has to be a clear understanding of what the expectations are. [Helsingborg, May 22, 2026 — Rutte-Rubio bilateral joint appearance, Day 2 of the emergency NATO Foreign Ministers Meeting. Rubio also noted Trump and senior officials remain 'very disappointed' with NATO over the alliance's Iran war response and Spain's denial of base access at Morón and Rota during Operation Epic Fury. May 14–15: 'What's the purpose of the alliance?' — the question that defined the ministerial's backdrop.]

name: Pete Hegseth
quote: The United States will no longer subsidize the defense of wealthy European nations. The era of the US bearing disproportionate cost for Europe's security is over. Model allies — Poland, Finland, the Baltics — who spend and step up will receive special favor. Those who failed to step up will face consequences. [May 30, 2026: renewed burden-sharing ultimatum as US prepares formal NATO withdrawal plan expected for June submission ahead of Ankara Leaders' Summit July 7–8. The formal plan will codify 10,200+ troop reductions and hardware cuts — jets −⅓, bombers −½, zero submarines, zero drones — disclosed by Pentagon adviser Velez-Green on May 26 (Der Spiegel).]

name: Péter Magyar
quote: Hungary will reappear as a strong NATO and EU ally. We will remove the vetoes on Ukraine's path to NATO membership, re-engage on EU burden-sharing, and rebuild Hungary's credibility as a constructive alliance partner.

name: Pedro Sánchez
quote: The position of the government of Spain is clear: absolute collaboration with the allies, but always within the framework of international legality. Spain is a committed NATO ally — we will not be intimidated by threats.

name: Radosław Sikorski
quote: We certainly hope so — but Article 5 doesn't say that you have to go to war. It says an attack on one is treated as an attack on all. NATO has survived crises of non-participation before.

name: Maria Malmer Stenergard
role: Swedish Foreign Minister (2022–present) / Helsingborg NATO FMM Chair
quote: Hosting a high-level meeting for the Alliance is a demonstration of Sweden's ambitions to be an active and constructive NATO Ally. [May 18, 2026: co-held pre-ministerial press briefing with PM Kristersson at Rosenbad — T-3 before the Helsingborg FMM. Sweden hosts its first NATO ministerial since joining in March 2024. Malmer Stenergard will formally chair the May 21–22 sessions as host-country FM. Airspace restrictions activated over Helsingborg for the duration of the summit.]

name: Anders Fogh Rasmussen
role: NATO Secretary General (2009–2014) / Former Danish Prime Minister
quote: What we are witnessing now is the disintegration of NATO, and this is dangerous. Trump has sown so much doubt about his commitment to Article 5 and the defense of Europe that there can only be one conclusion for Europeans: we must stand on our own feet. We need a coalition of willing nations — those who meet 5% GDP, commit to genuine collective defense, and cannot be vetoed by a single member.
